# A module's switch: variant generations, the C's Rust library, and the C test gate

Status: `open`.

## Signal

Procedures worked out by hand that the skills should state, met at the campaign's first
switch from C (`modules/libgit2/src/util/utf8.c/integration/run-1`), which every later switch
repeats, and two gaps where following the skills as written fails:

1. **The variants cannot be rebuilt in place.** `porting-workflow`'s Builds section rebuilds
   the shared variants "from the C that remains once the integration lands", and
   `testing-builds` has them prebuilt and immutable. Each variant's `configure` takes the C
   from the base checkout (`cmake -S ../../../c`), whose `c/` the batches still running hold
   with the module as C: three agents were building and testing against
   `crustify/builds` while this switch ran. A build configured from the integration
   worktree's `c/` instead is bound to a tree that is purged once the module integrates,
   and its build files then name sources that no longer exist.
2. **Campaign mode cannot build the Rust library the C links.** The C consumers link "the
   safe crate's Rust static library, built in campaign mode so that it carries no C of its
   own", but campaign mode (`bindgen`, Build modes) requires the variant's artifacts and
   static archive, which exist only once the C has linked, and the C's link needs the Rust
   library first. Once the C links it, the link edges campaign mode reads list it among
   their libraries, so the Rust tests would link the Rust twice, once from their rlib and once
   from the library.
3. **BorrowSanitizer has no `rustc` subcommand**, and `cargo bsan build` cannot override a
   crate's type, so the instrumented `staticlib` the `bsan` variant's C links has no direct
   command; its driver also bundles BSan's C runtime into the library, which the C's own link
   already links.
4. **The C test gate was scratch.** The baseline's per-suite runner,
   `crustify/tmp/scripts/c-suites.sh` in the base checkout, is untracked and writes its
   results into the variant's dir; a switch's gate compares with that baseline on every
   variant, at every switch.

The second switch, `src/cli/opt.c`'s (`modules/git2/src/cli/opt.c/integration/run-1`), the
first of the `git2` link unit, the CLI, ran items 1 to 4's scripts unchanged and met five
more gaps:

5. **A link unit no C test reaches has its switch gate in a module pass's run dir.** The
   CLI's exports are checked by running the relinked `git2` beside the previous one (the
   `git2`-exports lesson), but the comparison is `cli-smoke.py`, a scratch script recorded in
   `wave-186/batch-7/run-1`'s artifacts, which writes to a fixed `crustify/tmp/cli` and whose
   scratch commits take the clock's time, so that two runs' outputs differ in every line that
   prints a commit's date or id.
6. **Retiring a module's equivalence tests by file loses those that run no C.**
   `porting-workflow` retires them "which need the C", and keeps their behaviour in unit
   tests, but an equivalence file also holds tests that only read the raw bindings'
   constants, which stay with the header: two of `opt.c`'s did, and no unit test kept what
   they established.
7. **A review's reproducer that enables the deleted export feature no longer resolves.**
   Two reproducers under `crustify/reviews/modules/git2/src/cli/opt.c/wave-186/` name
   `ffi-export-src-cli-opt-c` in their manifests; nothing says whether a switch updates them
   or leaves them reproducing at the commit their report names.
8. **`build-variants.sh` takes no job count.** It builds every variant side by side, each
   `cmake --build` and `cargo` at the environment's job count, so a host cap holds only if
   the caller divides it by hand.
9. **The C library's link pulls Rust it never calls.** With `opt.rs`'s gateway compiled,
   `libgit2.so`, which calls only `utf8.c`'s exports, holds 6337 local Rust functions where
   gen1's held 2608, and imports about 75 more glibc functions: the linker takes whole
   archive members of the dev-profile `staticlib`, and does not collect unused sections.
   Its exported API does not change.

The third switch, `deps/llhttp/api.c`'s (`modules/libgit2/deps/llhttp/api.c/integration/run-1`),
ran items 1 to 4's scripts unchanged and met four more gaps:

10. **The switch's Rust side precedes the generation.** It is the first switch that removes
    raw bindings: 23 functions without an export, with their allowlist entries. Each
    variant's `build` runs `rust-staticlib.sh`, which builds the crate of the checkout with
    `--features bindgen` in campaign mode, checking the committed bindings against the
    variant's headers, and compiles the gateway only once the export feature is gone. So the
    switch's Rust side, the feature deleted, the allowlist pruned and the bindings
    regenerated, comes before `build-variants.sh`, not after the C's removal as the
    procedure's order (the C change, then the variants, then the gates) suggests. The
    bindings are regenerated against the previous generation, whose headers the switch does
    not change.
11. **A module whose exports only an online suite reaches has no C gate.** `c-tests.sh` runs
    the offline suites the baseline records, and no offline C test drives libgit2's HTTP
    client (the module pass's finding): `httpparser.c`, `httpclient.c` and `llhttp.c`'s
    generated parser call the 31 exports only in a fetch, clone or push over HTTP, whose
    suites (`online::*`) the baseline disables, since they need the network. libgit2's own CI
    runs part of them offline, against servers on localhost named by `GITTEST_REMOTE_URL`
    (`ci/test.sh`'s `auth_clone_and_push`, `-sonline::clone::push -sonline::push`).
12. **The equivalence tests that call no C are marked already.** Item 6's step needs each
    retiring test's calls checked. A test that calls C carries `#[cfg_attr(miri, ignore =
    "calls C")]` (the Miri gate's marker), so the tests that lack it are the candidates, a
    mechanical check; here all 21 carry it, and none is carried over.
13. **A CMake file may name the removed source in a property.** `deps/llhttp/CMakeLists.txt`
    globs its sources, as the lesson has it, and also sets
    `set_source_files_properties(api.c http.c llhttp.c PROPERTIES COMPILE_FLAGS …)`. CMake
    ignores a property of a source no target lists, so the file was left unchanged and every
    variant configured and built; the dangling name stays until the last of the three goes.

## Evidence

The run's commits `012d1d34c` (the switch), and the fork's `1b37e3d08`; its dashboard Notes
entry, `libgit2/src/util/utf8.c` integration. Where the run went:

- Item 1: the variants were rebuilt as `crustify/builds.gen1`, a directory beside
  `crustify/builds`, which the integration worktree's `crustify/builds` links to, each
  configured from `crustify/builds.gen1/c`, a detached worktree of the fork at the commit the
  generation was built from (`crustify/scripts/build-variants.sh`). The side campaigns'
  installs, reached as `$PWD/../../../..`, resolve the same from a sibling of `builds`.
- Item 2: `build.rs`'s campaign mode takes `CRUSTIFY_STATICLIB`, under which it reads the
  variant's configured build (`build.ninja`, `CMakeCache.txt` and `libgit2.pc`, all written
  by `configure`) and links none of it, and every other campaign build leaves out of the link
  the library the build's cache names (`LIBGIT2_RUST_LIBRARY`), matched by canonical path,
  since CMake names it relative to the build dir and the cache by its physical path.
  `crustify/scripts/rust-staticlib.sh` runs as the first step of each variant's `build`,
  between `configure` and `cmake --build`. The library carries only the Rust, its three
  exports and the crate's own `__extern` wrappers (`nm`): campaign mode links the variant's
  archive unbundled (`static:-bundle`), so a `staticlib` leaves it out.
- Item 3: a stand-in for the cargo that cargo-bsan runs (`CARGO`) turns its `build` into
  `rustc --crate-type staticlib`, every other call passing through, and the bundled runtime's
  90 members are removed from the copy written; the `bsan` variant's `libgit2.so` then holds
  no `__bsan_*` definition, and its `util_tests -sutf8` passes.
- Item 4: `crustify/scripts/c-tests.sh` runs `build.json`'s `test` command over a copy of the
  variant's `CTestTestfile.cmake` tree, and every suite alone as the baseline did, into an
  output dir of its own, and compares the tally with `c-baseline.json`'s record.

Where `src/cli/opt.c`'s switch went (its commits on the module's branch, the fork's
`f57e1a616`, and its dashboard Notes entry, `git2/src/cli/opt.c` integration):

- Items 1 to 4: `build-variants.sh` built `crustify/builds.gen2` from `f57e1a616`, five
  variants in about 15 minutes, each archive holding 211 objects where gen1's held 212,
  `opt.c.o` gone, and each `git2` defining the five `cli_opt_*` exports as global Rust
  symbols (gen1's were the C's local ones). The CLI's link unit needed no change of its own:
  the first switch's `SelectRust.cmake` already links the library into the CLI, which takes
  libgit2's objects statically, and the crate's default features include `git2`, so
  `rust-staticlib.sh`'s library already carries the CLI's exports once its feature is gone.
  `c-tests.sh` ran unchanged.
- Item 5: the switch ran `cli-smoke.py` from the module pass's run dir, the stock `git2` being
  gen1's and the relinked one gen2's, on plain, ASan/UBSan and TSan: 62 of 66 the same on
  each, the 4 others the module's recorded departures, and no sanitizer report. Gen2's
  outcomes equal the module pass's relinked ones on all 66, but for three (`cat-file -p HEAD`,
  `cat-file commit HEAD`, `blame f1`) that differ only in the scratch commit's date and id.
  A tracked script beside `c-tests.sh`, taking its output dir and the command lines' file,
  with `GIT_AUTHOR_DATE` and `GIT_COMMITTER_DATE` fixed, would make each run's record
  comparable with the last.
- Item 6: `usage_flags_match_the_c_constants` and `parse_flags_match_the_c_constants`, which
  compared `Usage`'s and `ParseFlags`' bits with `opt.h`'s `CLI_OPT_USAGE_*` and
  `CLI_OPT_PARSE_*` through the raw bindings, moved to `tests/unit_pub/src/cli/opt.rs`; the
  CLI's spec tables, which stay C, set those bits. The switch's step would read: before an
  equivalence file is retired, each of its tests that calls no C is carried over to the
  module's unit tests.
- Item 7: the two reproducers were left as they are, reproducing at the commit their reports
  name.
- Item 8: the switch split the host's cap of 48 by hand, `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=10` and
  `CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL=10` for the five variants.
- Item 9: `nm` of each generation's plain `libgit2.so.1.9.0`: 5878 and 9607 local and global
  text symbols, 2608 and 6337 of them Rust's (`_R`), `cli_opt_parse` in neither; the dynamic
  symbol tables differ only in undefined glibc imports. `-Wl,--gc-sections` on the link that
  takes the Rust library, or a library built with one codegen unit per export, would keep it
  to what the C calls; not tried.

Where `deps/llhttp/api.c`'s switch went (its commits on the module's branch, the fork's
`c54c0c180`, and its dashboard Notes entry, `libgit2/deps/llhttp/api.c` integration):

- Items 1 to 4: `build-variants.sh` built `crustify/builds.gen3` from `c54c0c180`, five
  variants in about 7 minutes at 12 jobs each (item 8's split again, for the 64 the run was
  capped at), each archive holding 210 objects where gen2's held 211, `api.c.o` gone. In
  every variant, `libgit2.so`, `git2` and `libgit2_tests` define the 31 exports (`addr2line`
  puts `llhttp_execute` at `api.rs:1634`) and none of api.c's 23 unexported functions; each
  passed its smoke test (`util_tests -sutf8`). `libgit2.so` defines the same 907 dynamic
  symbols as gen2's, and holds 6747 local Rust functions where gen2's held 6337 (item 9).
  `c-tests.sh` ran unchanged.
- Item 10: the run deleted the feature, pruned `sys/libgit2/allowlist.txt` of the 23
  functions and regenerated `bindings.rs` (`CRUSTIFY_BINDINGS_UPDATE=1 cargo-variant.sh plain
  build --features bindgen --lib`, against gen2), committed that, and only then committed the
  C change and ran `build-variants.sh`, whose `rust-staticlib.sh` then checked the committed
  bindings against gen3's headers on every variant.
- Item 11: the run added `crustify/scripts/http-remote.py`, `git http-backend` behind a
  persistent HTTP/1.1 front that frames each response by its path (`Content-Length`,
  chunked in 1, 7, 4096 and 65536-byte chunks, chunked with chunk extensions, or
  close-delimited), with an optional Basic challenge, and `crustify/scripts/http-gate.sh`,
  which runs a variant's `git2 clone` of two repositories through each framing, three
  clones that fail, and `libgit2_tests -sonline::push -sonline::clone::credentials` with
  `GITTEST_REMOTE_URL` at the guarded remote, into a `results.txt` free of times, ports and
  paths. Gen2's and gen3's results are compared with `diff` (the dashboard entry).
- Item 12: `grep -c 'ignore = "calls C"'` over `tests/equiv/deps/llhttp/api.rs` gives 21,
  its `#[test]` count; the module pass's map (`wave-194/batch-7`'s `misc` report) names the
  unit tests that keep each.
- Item 13: `deps/llhttp/CMakeLists.txt` unchanged; gen3's five `configure`s and builds
  passed with it.
- Item 7 again: `wave-194/batch-7/equiv/execute-export-moves-an-empty-runs-error-pos`'s
  reproducer names `ffi-export-deps-llhttp-api-c`, and is left reproducing at the commit its
  report names.

## Destination

The spec, where `authoring` places each part, with the scripts beside the skills that name
them, generalized from libgit2's names (`libgit2_tests`, `util_tests`, the
`LIBGIT2_RUST_LIBRARY` variable, the `offline` and `util` targets) into arguments:

- `setup`, Builds, and `testing-builds`, Builds: the variants are built in generations, each
  from a worktree of the fork of its own, and a checkout's `crustify/builds` links to one; a
  switch builds the next generation, and the assistant moves the base checkout to it once
  the switch lands, so that the batches in flight keep theirs. `build-variants.sh` beside
  `setup`.
- `bindgen`, Build modes: the `staticlib` form of campaign mode, and that campaign mode leaves
  the library the C links out of its own links.
- `testing-builds`, Builds: each variant's C consumers link a library built with its
  instrumentation, by `rust-staticlib.sh`, including BSan's form above.
- `testing-gates`, Regressions: a switch's C tests run by `c-tests.sh` per variant the
  baseline records, compared with it.
- `porting-workflow`, Builds: the order a switch's steps take, the C build's `configure`
  before the Rust library and its link after it.
- `porting-workflow`, One language per module (item 6): an equivalence test that calls no C
  is carried over to the module's unit tests at the switch, not retired with the file.
- `testing-gates`, Regressions (item 5): a link unit that no C test reaches is checked at its
  switch by its relinked executables beside the previous generation's, by a tracked script
  beside `c-tests.sh`, and the result compared with the module pass's record.
- `reviewing` (item 7): whether a switch updates the reproducers that name its export
  feature.
- `build-variants.sh` (item 8): a job count, divided among the variants it builds.
- `bindgen`, Build modes, or the fork's `SelectRust.cmake` (item 9): the C library's link
  collects the Rust it does not call.
- `porting-workflow`, Builds (item 10): the switch's Rust side, the bindings regenerated,
  lands before the generation is built, since every variant's build checks them.
- `testing-gates`, Regressions (item 11): a switch whose exports only the baseline's disabled
  online suites reach runs those the target's own CI runs against local servers, against a
  local remote, by the scripts beside `c-tests.sh`, on the new generation and the previous
  one, compared; `http-remote.py` and `http-gate.sh` generalized from libgit2's suites and
  variables into arguments.
- `porting-workflow`, One language per module (item 12): the carry-over candidates are the
  retiring tests without the Miri `calls C` marker.
- The `libgit2` CMake lesson (item 13): a property naming the removed file is left.

## Change

Made in the campaign only: the scripts under `crustify/scripts/`, `build.rs`'s campaign
mode and `build.json` version 7, and, from `deps/llhttp/api.c`'s switch, `http-remote.py`
and `http-gate.sh` beside `c-tests.sh`. The skills are not changed by this run: the change spans
`setup`, `bindgen`, `testing-builds` and `testing-gates`, which are not the translator's to
evolve, and wants its own review.

## Validation

This run: `build-variants.sh` built the five variants of `crustify/builds.gen1` from the
fork's `1b37e3d08`, each smoke-tested (`util_tests -sutf8`); the workspace's gates ran over
them and `c-tests.sh` compared four variants with the baseline, as the dashboard entry
records. A later switch validates the generalized scripts by running them.

`src/cli/opt.c`'s switch ran `build-variants.sh`, `rust-staticlib.sh` and `c-tests.sh`
unchanged, for a second link unit, and its gates over `crustify/builds.gen2` are its
dashboard entry's. Items 5 to 9 are its evidence, and are not made: `porting-workflow` is the
translator's to evolve, but item 6 wants review with the rest of this proposal.

`deps/llhttp/api.c`'s switch ran the three scripts unchanged again, for a third module, the
first whose exports libgit2 itself calls only over the network. Its gates over
`crustify/builds.gen3` are its dashboard entry's. Item 11's two scripts are made, in the
campaign only (`crustify/scripts/http-remote.py` and `http-gate.sh`), and validated by that
run: gen2's C and gen3's Rust give the same `results.txt` on plain, ASan+UBSan and TSan, and on
gen3's coverage variant the run calls 24 of the 31 exports. A mutant of an export was not
built, so whether the comparison catches a departure rests on the coverage alone. Items 10,
12 and 13 are evidence, and are not made: they want review with the rest of this proposal.

## Review

### `libgit2/src/util/utf8.c` wave 229 batch 0: the module's `port`

The module's whole `port`, the items of waves 229 to 231 folded into one batch, since each
depends on the one before: `glb::utf8proc_utf8class`, `fn::utf8_charlen`,
`fn::git_utf8_iterate`, `fn::git_utf8_char_length` and `fn::git_utf8_valid_buf_length`, in
`src/libgit2/src/util/utf8.rs`. The table is a `static` built by a `const fn` from its lead
byte ranges, which a `unit_priv` test checks against C's literal; `utf8_charlen` is the
private `sequence_len(&[u8]) -> Option<usize>`; the three functions are the native
`decode_char(&[u8]) -> Result<(char, usize), InvalidCodePoint>`, `char_count(&[u8]) -> usize`
and `valid_prefix_len(&[u8]) -> usize`. What `git_utf8_iterate` accepts is always a scalar
value, so the code point is a `char`. One C defect is not carried over: with `str_len` 0,
`utf8_charlen` skips its bound check and `git_utf8_iterate` reads past the size it is given;
no caller passes 0 (`next_hfs_char` loops while `*len`), and the port and its export refuse
empty bytes (-1, `*out` 0), documented on both and kept by a unit test. No out-of-tree
entity is used.

The crate's first `ffi_export` gateway, under the crate's first export feature,
`ffi-export-src-util-utf8-c`, declared off in `Cargo.toml`: `git_utf8_iterate`,
`git_utf8_char_length` and `git_utf8_valid_buf_length`, under their C names, for
`path.c`'s `next_hfs_char`, `diff_xdiff.c`'s `git_xdiff_cb` and, on Windows, `fs_path.c`,
whose `port/unexport` stages are waves 232, 860 and 1531. Each body runs in ffibox's
`barrier`, a panic reported as -1 by `git_utf8_iterate` and aborting the two that cannot
fail, and each export is checked against its raw binding by a constant, `[sys::<name>,
<name>]`, whose function items coerce to one pointer type only where the signatures agree:
`str_len: u32` in an export fails to build (`E0308`). The three functions were allowlisted
(`wrapper.h` gains `utf8.h`) for that check and the equivalence tests. As a scratch check,
not a gate, the feature on links the exports in place of the archive's `utf8.o` (no
`utf8proc_utf8class` in the binary, C's `next_hfs_char` resolving to Rust): the six `equiv`
tests then compare the gateway with the native API and pass, and so do the tests of
`path.c` and `diff_xdiff.c`. The pointer findings of the four functions are submitted to
the ownership store.

Tests: four `unit_priv` tests (the table against C's, empty bytes, every lead byte's class,
broken continuations), eleven `unit_pub` tests, three doctests and six `equiv` tests (the
cases of `test_utf8__char_length` and the boundaries, every lead byte followed by every kind
of byte, every byte pair, every three-byte sequence, every `char`'s encoding and the
four-byte forms past U+10FFFF, and walks that compare after each step).
`char_count_carries_over_the_c_test` carries over the module's one C test case,
`test_utf8__char_length`, unchanged.

Coverage: `run.sh` on a `git archive` of the wave tip `2216b0cd0` and on this tree, read
with `report.py` from each scratch tree's `src/libgit2` (`coverage-report-relative-rows`),
the unit column merging `lib` and `unit_pub`. Worklist: Rust `utf8.rs` 58 of 59 lines, 83 of
84 regions and 14 of 14 functions, the one line `decode_char`'s `_` arm, which no length
`sequence_len` returns reaches; the gateway is compiled out. C `utf8.c` 69 of 71 lines, 54
of 55 regions and 4 of 4 functions under `equiv` (40 of 71 at the tip), the two lines
`git_utf8_iterate`'s unreachable `default: return -1`; its own C test reaches
`git_utf8_char_length` alone. The tree was measured twice, the second after a test was made
to call the table's `const fn` at run time, which coverage did not count when only the
compiler evaluated it; the C total moved `45.02`% to `44.97`% between the two runs with the
C unchanged, run-to-run variation, as are the `ub_safe` and `ub_unsafe` C shifts, which this
batch's tests do not run. The Overview's Rust LoC moves by ffimap's `code.loc.total`
(`+132`) and `code.tests.loc.total` (`+357`). `+LoC` leaves out the regenerated
`bindings.rs` (`+41`), as earlier rows do. The `loc` cell is wavefront's `query dag --loc`.

The safety audit scans (ffimap `9aa2ef1`, flags as wave 225's) name the export feature on
this tree, the only one not yet switched, and none on the tip, which declares none: `raw→std`
`+1` is the gateway's `slice::from_raw_parts`, and `unsafe blocks` `+1` its `bytes` helper,
the exports' four blocks being `ffi_export`'s. The boundary scan's sites hold none in the
changeset. `ffimap api` over the worklist: the three exported functions `new`; the table
and `utf8_charlen` are private, so `missing`; unattributed, the new `utf8` module
(`InvalidCodePoint`) and `sys::libgit2` extended by the three bindings.

Gates, on the base `2216b0cd0`, which the wave branch still pointed at: formatted, and
`clippy --all-targets` passes with warnings denied with the export feature off and on. The
whole workspace passes on `plain` (`lib` 844 and 1 ignored, `ub_safe` 762, `ub_unsafe` 120,
`equiv` 534, `unit_pub` 78, `hidden_symbols` 1, doctests 75 merged and 378 standalone). The
tests of `util::utf8`, `libgit2::path` and `diff_xdiff` pass under ASan+UBSan. Miri passes
the new `unit_priv`, `unit_pub` and doctests; the six `equiv` tests, each run alone, stop at
`git_utf8_iterate` or `git_utf8_char_length` (`calls libgit2`). TSan and BSan have no
obligation: no `Send` or `Sync` claim, no thread, and no test the batch expects to trigger
BSan. The raw bindings changed, so the crate was packaged: `cargo package` cannot resolve
the unpublished `glibc-bindings`, so it was packaged with `--no-verify --exclude-lockfile`,
and the extracted package, given its own workspace and `[patch.crates-io]` entries for
`glibc-bindings` and `ffibox`, builds alone in bundled mode with no variant, the side
campaigns' `plain` installs on `OPENSSL_ROOT_DIR` and `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH`
(`crustify/evolution/package-gate-procedure`). Usage cells are the assistant's.

### `libgit2/src/util/utf8.c` wave 229 batch 1: module pass

The module pass, and the module's only review, over batch 0's three paths (`680ac73bf`), for
every objective with `fix`. The module files no finding of its own. `decode_char`,
`char_count` and `valid_prefix_len` are `git_utf8_iterate`'s, `git_utf8_char_length`'s and
`git_utf8_valid_buf_length`'s results for every input but `str_len` 0, where C reads past
its size and the port refuses, as its docs and a unit test say. The class table is
utf8proc's, and the anchors, homes and placement follow the conventions. The ownership
store's pointer blocks for the four functions hold against the C. `test_utf8__char_length`'s
ten assertions are all carried over, unchanged, by `char_count_carries_over_the_c_test`, so
no case of the module's one C test is left uncarried. That test uses only the module's
exports, so it stays after the switch.

The gateway was reviewed for what the C that stays relies on. `next_hfs_char` needs a
length no larger than `*len` and the code point written. `git_xdiff_cb` needs a prefix no
longer than its header, cut before a sequence its size splits, and `fs_path.c` needs the
count. None passes `str_len` 0. The exports keep each, and a panic cannot unwind into C.
The export feature on, `fmt` and `clippy --all-targets` pass with warnings denied. With the
exports linked in place of C's `utf8.o`, the whole workspace passes on `plain` and passes
under ASan+UBSan but for the known nightly failures. That link used a private build under
`crustify/tmp/`, whose copy of the archive lacks `utf8.c.o`, named by `CRUSTIFY_BUILD_DIR`.
`nm` shows no `utf8proc_utf8class`, and `next_hfs_char` and `git_xdiff_cb` call Rust. As a
scratch check, C's own suites ran too: the variant's `libgit2_tests` and `util_tests` were
relinked from their `build.ninja` edges, against the crate built as a `staticlib` with the
feature, in place of `src/util`'s `utf8.c.o`. `util_tests` passed whole, `-sutf8` included.
`libgit2_tests -spath -sdiff -sindex -scheckout -srefs` matched the stock binary: 825
passed, 22 skipped. That procedure is proposed for the `port` batches' gates
(`crustify/evolution/export-link-check`). The gateway had no test (`test-adequacy`): its
region gains four `unit_priv` tests, which compile with it, under the feature until the
switch. They check the code point and length written or the refusal's 0 and -1, a
`next_hfs_char` walk, the two counts, and that `str_len` 0 reads nothing, NULL or dangling.
Each input sits in an allocation of exactly its size. The four pass on `plain`, under
ASan+UBSan with the exports linked, and under Miri. Two mutants fail them: `bytes()`
reading one byte more fails under Miri, and a refusal writing `u32::MAX` fails the
assertions. `git_utf8_iterate`'s `# Safety` now asks for an aligned `out`.

The module's end gates found the pass's one finding, outside the module:
`ub_safe/first-filter-loads-race-on-builtin-filter-flags`. TSan failed `lib` on the tip with
libgit2's `filter_initialize` race. A `checkout` fixture staged files through
`git_index_add_bypath` while a `blob` test initialised the filters. libgit2 writes a filter's
`initialized` flag under only its registry's read lock, and the crate closed that for
`filter.rs`'s constructors alone. A `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` reproducer races two threads'
`hash_file` calls and exits 66, five runs of five. The fix has `runtime_pinned`, which every
safe constructor passes, call `initialise_builtin_filters`. The helper now only looks `crlf`
and `ident` up, which initialises them without allocating. A first version kept its scratch
list, and the list's 145 and 192 bytes failed eleven allocator-tracing `equiv` tests. The
reproducer exits 0, and its regression test, `ub_safe`'s
`filter::first_loads_on_two_threads_do_not_race`, fails under TSan without the call. Its
`disclosure.md` is for libgit2's issue tracker. Filing a gate's true positive outside the
workset is proposed for `reviewing` (`crustify/evolution/gate-findings-outside-the-workset`,
crustify `1423c7f`, awaiting review).

Gates ran on `end-gates` snapshots under the worktree's `crustify/tmp/`, at 24 jobs, without
BSan (the settings' `sanitizers` answer). On the tip `680ac73bf`: plain passes the whole
workspace (`lib` 844 and 1 ignored, `equiv` 534, `ub_safe` 762, `ub_unsafe` 120, `unit_pub`
78, `hidden_symbols` 1, doctests 75 and 378). ASan+UBSan passes it but for the known
`compile_fail` snapshots and `CommitBuilder` doctest. TSan fails those and `lib`, with the
race above. Miri passes every binary (`lib` 396, `ub_safe` 194, `equiv` 38, `unit_pub` 43,
`ub_unsafe` 19 passed, the rest marked). On the landed tree, plain passes the whole
workspace, `ub_safe` 763. ASan+UBSan and TSan pass it but for the known failures, `lib`
included under TSan. Miri passes every binary as on the tip, `ub_safe`'s new test marked (`calls libgit2`).

Coverage: `run.sh` on a `git archive` of the tip and on this tree, read with `report.py` from
each scratch tree's `src/libgit2`, the unit column merging `lib` and `unit_pub`. The totals
move from `44.99`% / `98.81`% on the tip to `44.98`% / `98.82`%. The tip measures `44.99`%,
where batch 0 recorded `44.97`% for the same tree, so each suite's shift of a few hundredths
is within run-to-run variation. The first pin's filter lookups add C lines to every suite.
The gateway's tests compile out with the feature off, so the worklist's figures are batch
0's, and its tests count `+0`. The safety audit scan (ffimap `9aa2ef1`, batch 0's flags, the
export feature on) differs from batch 0's in `FFI calls` and `unsafe blocks` `-3` each,
which are the scratch list's three calls. The Overview's LoC moves by `code.loc.total` (`-2`)
and `code.tests.loc.total` (`+114`). `ffimap api` over the worklist: the three functions are
`kept`, the table and `utf8_charlen` `missing`, every unattributed module `kept`. No raw
binding or C changed, so the packaging gate does not apply. Usage cells are the
assistant's.


### `libgit2/src/util/utf8.c` integration: the switch from C

The campaign's first switch, run by `modules/libgit2/src/util/utf8.c/integration/run-1` on the
module's branch after the merge of the working branch (`43605086f`): `012d1d34c`, and the
fork's `1b37e3d08`. The export feature `ffi-export-src-util-utf8-c` is deleted, the crate's
only one, so `utf8.rs`'s gateway compiles from now on, and its four `unit_priv` tests run in
`lib`. The module's six `equiv` tests are retired with the C they compared
(`tests/equiv/src/util/utf8.rs`); their cases stay in its unit tests and doctests. The raw
bindings of `git_utf8_iterate`, `git_utf8_char_length` and `git_utf8_valid_buf_length` stay,
and now reach the exports. `src/util/utf8.c` leaves `c/`: the change is the commit
`integrate src/util/utf8.c` on a local `fork/main`, which stands for
`crustify-rs/libgit2-fork`'s `main` and is not pushed, and `.gitmodules` names the fork.
`utf8.h` stays for `path.c`, `diff_xdiff.c` and `fs_path.c`. The module's tied C test,
`tests/util/utf8.c`, calls `git_utf8_char_length` alone, so it stays and checks the export.
No C test leaves, so no case needs listing. The exports are a private module's, so the
crate's API does not change.

The switch also made the one-time change of the C build. The fork's
`cmake/SelectRust.cmake` links the static library that `LIBGIT2_RUST_LIBRARY` names wherever
the remaining C is linked: `libgit2.so`, the CLI, `libgit2_tests` and `util_tests`. It is an
imported target among `LIBGIT2_SYSTEM_LIBS`. `libgit2.so` keeps the Rust's symbols local
(`--exclude-libs`). Its dynamic symbols are the previous generation's on every variant,
`asan-ubsan`'s two linker-made `__start_`/`__stop_asan_globals` aside. Those come from LLVM
23's instrumentation of the Rust and are protected. Without the variable, the library leaves
the three exports undefined, as the crate's bundled and shared builds of `c/` need. Each
variant's `build` command first makes the library (`crustify/scripts/rust-staticlib.sh`),
between `configure` and the C's link. It builds the crate of the checkout that runs it as a
`staticlib` on the dev profile, the profile the Rust tests run on, so that the C tests check
the same build with debug assertions and overflow checks on. It builds in campaign mode
against the configured variant, with `--features bindgen`, so that the committed bindings
are checked, and with `CRUSTIFY_STATICLIB`, under which `build.rs` reads the build's
configuration and links none of its C. It instruments the Rust as `cargo-variant.sh` does.
`nm` shows that the library defines only the Rust, the three exports and the crate's
`__extern` wrappers, and no libgit2 C. Every other campaign build leaves the library out of
its link, matched by canonical path, so that no binary holds the Rust twice. BSan has no
`cargo bsan rustc`, so a stand-in for the cargo it runs turns its `build` into `rustc
--crate-type staticlib`. The BSan runtime its driver bundles is removed from the copy, since
the variant's C link links it.

The variants were rebuilt as a new generation, `crustify/builds.gen1`, with
`crustify/scripts/build-variants.sh`, and this worktree's `crustify/builds` links to it.
`crustify/builds` itself, which three batches were using, was left untouched. Each variant is
configured from the generation's own `c`, a detached worktree of the fork at `1b37e3d08`, so
that the build outlives this worktree and the base checkout's next moves (`build.json`
version 7). Each archive holds 212 objects, where the previous generation's held 213:
`utf8.c.o` is gone. Each variant passed its smoke test (`util_tests -sutf8`). In every
variant, `utf8proc_utf8class` is absent from the C test executables, which take
`git_utf8_iterate` from the Rust; in `libgit2.so` it is a local symbol.

Gates on `012d1d34c`, over gen1, from `end-gates` snapshots at 24 jobs. The workspace is
formatted, and `clippy --workspace --all-targets` passes with warnings denied. Plain passes
the whole workspace: `lib` 848 and 1 ignored, `equiv` 528, `ub_safe` 763, `ub_unsafe` 120,
`unit_pub` 84, `hidden_symbols` 1, doctests 76 and 378. ASan+UBSan and TSan pass it but for
the known nightly failures: the 9 `compile_fail` snapshots and the `CommitBuilder` doctest
(E0624). Miri passes every binary: `lib` 400, `ub_safe` 194, `equiv` 38, `unit_pub` 49,
`ub_unsafe` 19, the rest marked. The remaining C tests ran over the link with the Rust,
through `crustify/scripts/c-tests.sh`. It runs `build.json`'s `ctest` command, then every
suite alone as the baseline did, and compares the result with `c-baseline.json`. Plain,
ASan+UBSan and TSan give 3443 passed and 55 skipped of 3498, coverage 3444 and 54, each the
baseline's record. Under TSan, the same 10 suites as the baseline's report the C's
lock-order inversions and races, and no case fails; no report has a Rust frame. `ctest`
passes both targets on plain, ASan+UBSan and coverage. Under TSan it fails `offline` on those
reports alone, 49 lock-order inversions and glibc's `tzset` race. BSan was rebuilt and not
run, as the settings' `sanitizers` answer has it. `c/` changed, so the crate was packaged as
`package-gate-procedure` has it. The package has 697 files, `utf8.c` out and
`SelectRust.cmake` in, and builds alone in bundled mode. Its `libgit2.pc`'s
`Requires.private` also needs the side campaigns' installs on `PKG_CONFIG_PATH`, beside
`CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH`. Its `lib` tests link, `path.c`'s `next_hfs_char` calling the Rust export.
790 pass, among them the module's; the other 58 need the fixture repositories of
`c/tests/resources`, which the package leaves out.

From the switch on, the module's coverage is its Rust's: `utf8.c` is in no build, and the C
figures lose its 71 lines. This run did not measure coverage. The procedure this switch
worked out, which every later switch repeats, is proposed for the spec
(`crustify/evolution/module-switch-procedure`). That libgit2's switch removes a file and no
CMake line is a lesson. Usage cells are the assistant's.

### `libgit2/deps/ntlmclient/compat.h` wave 200 batch 0: `MIN`

`deps/ntlmclient/compat.h` is a header with no translation unit, and its one scheduled item is
`#define MIN(x, y) (((x) < (y)) ? (x) : (y))`, under `#ifndef MIN`; the header's `bool`,
`true` and `false` are defined only under `_MSC_VER`. `mac::MIN` is the native
`fn min<T: PartialOrd>(x: T, y: T) -> T` in `src/libgit2/deps/ntlmclient/compat_h.rs`, the
macro's body over any `PartialOrd` type: ties and pairs `<` cannot order return `y`, as the C
does, and for an `Ord` type the result is `core::cmp::min`'s, the plan's `rust_equivalent`. It
is not a `const fn`, since a generic comparison cannot be called in a constant on stable Rust
1.100. Its docs name where it departs from the macro: one operand type rather than the usual
arithmetic conversions, and each operand evaluated once, where the macro evaluates the one

### `libgit2/deps/llhttp/api.c` integration: the switch from C

The campaign's third switch, run by `modules/libgit2/deps/llhttp/api.c/integration/run-1` on the
module's branch, after the merge of the working branch (`a4335ab7a`): `21c5c5f47`, and the fork's
`c54c0c180`. It followed the procedure of `utf8.c`'s and `opt.c`'s switches
(`crustify/evolution/module-switch-procedure`) with their scripts unchanged. The export feature
`ffi-export-deps-llhttp-api-c` is deleted, so `api.rs`'s gateway compiles from now on, and its
eight `unit_priv` tests run in `lib`. No export feature is left. The remaining C calls the 31
exports: `transports/httpparser.c` calls `llhttp_execute`, `llhttp_finish`,
`llhttp_get_error_pos` and `llhttp_resume_after_upgrade`, `httpparser.h`'s macros, which
`httpclient.c` expands, call `llhttp_init`, `llhttp_pause`, `llhttp_resume` and
`llhttp_get_error_reason`, and `llhttp.c`'s generated parser calls the 23 `llhttp__on_*`
dispatchers. The raw bindings of the eight functions stay and reach the exports. The dispatchers
have no header declaration and no raw binding. The 23 functions bound without an export go with
their allowlist entries: the seven getters, the three name functions, `llhttp_settings_init`,
`llhttp_reset`, `llhttp_set_error_reason` and the ten lenient setters. Only api.c's equivalence
tests called them, and `bindings.rs` was regenerated without them. Removing them changes the
crate's raw API, `sys::libgit2`, as the porting workflow's switch has it; the safe API does not
change. The types stay for the layouts `httpparser.c` and `llhttp.c` build and read.
`deps/llhttp/api.c` leaves `c/` on the local `fork/main` as `integrate deps/llhttp/api.c`,
which is not pushed. `llhttp.h` stays for `llhttp.c`, `http.c` and the HTTP client.
`deps/llhttp/CMakeLists.txt` globs its sources and is unchanged; its
`set_source_files_properties(api.c http.c llhttp.c …)` names the removed file, and CMake ignores
it. The module has no tied C test. The doc comment that counted nine functions C calls now says
eight.

The module's 21 `equiv` tests are retired with the C they compared (`tests/equiv/deps/llhttp/api.rs`
and its `mod api;`). Each calls C, api.c's own or `llhttp.c`'s parse through it, and carries the
Miri `calls C` marker, so none is carried over. The module pass (`wave-194/batch-7`'s `misc`
report) maps each to the unit tests that keep its behaviour. What none keeps is the
differential itself. The parser's private state was compared byte for byte with C's from six
states, and the lenient setters were shown to read any nonzero `int` as true. Once the C is gone,
nothing is left to compare with. `tests/equiv/deps/llhttp/llhttp.rs` stays: it compares
`llhttp.c`'s port with its C, whose parse now runs over the Rust dispatchers.

The Rust side landed before the variants were built: every variant's build runs
`rust-staticlib.sh`, which checks the committed bindings and compiles the gateway (proposal's
item 10). The variants were rebuilt as `crustify/builds.gen3` from `c54c0c180` with
`build-variants.sh`, at 12 jobs each so that the five stayed within the host's 64. This
worktree's `crustify/builds` links to gen3, and gen2 was left untouched. Each archive holds 210
objects where gen2's held 211, `api.c.o` gone. In every variant, `libgit2.so`, `git2` and
`libgit2_tests` define the 31 exports and none of api.c's 23 other functions. `addr2line` puts
`llhttp_execute` at `api.rs:1634`. Each variant passed its smoke test (`util_tests -sutf8`,
`git2 --version`). `libgit2.so`'s dynamic symbol table defines the same 907 symbols. It now
holds 6747 local Rust functions where gen2's held 6337 (proposal's item 9).

Gates, over gen3 from `end-gates` snapshots at 64 jobs. The workspace is formatted, and `clippy
--workspace --all-targets` passes with warnings denied. Plain passes the whole workspace:
`lib` 901 and 1 ignored, `equiv` 532, `ub_safe` 796, `ub_unsafe` 144, `unit_pub` 218,
`hidden_symbols` 1, doctests 101 and 397. ASan+UBSan and TSan pass it but for the known nightly
failures: the 9 `compile_fail` snapshots, the six `checkout_*`,
`diff_parse_options_no_raw_conversion`, `odb_options_no_raw_conversion` and
`progress_callback_not_send`, and the `CommitBuilder` doctest (E0624). Neither printed a
sanitizer report. The gateway's eight tests pass on plain, ASan+UBSan and TSan, the first time
under TSan. Miri passes every binary: `lib` 441, `ub_safe` 212, `unit_pub` 141, `equiv` 38,
`ub_unsafe` 26, the rest marked. The gateway's tests are among them: six pass, and
`llhttp_init_initialises_storage_and_stores_what_c_passes` and
`llhttp_execute_keeps_an_empty_runs_error_pos_at_data` are marked `calls C`. The remaining C
tests ran over the link with the Rust through `c-tests.sh`. Plain, ASan+UBSan and TSan give 3443
passed and 55 skipped of 3498, coverage 3444 and 54, each the baseline's record. Under TSan, the
same 10 suites as the baseline's report the C's lock-order inversions and races, and no case
fails; no report has a Rust frame. `ctest` passes both targets on plain, ASan+UBSan and
coverage. Under TSan it fails `offline` on those reports alone, 49 lock-order inversions and
glibc's `tzset` race, as at the two switches before. BSan was rebuilt and not run, as the
settings' `sanitizers` answer has it.

No offline C test drives the HTTP client, and the baseline disables the online suites. So this
switch checked the exports through libgit2's own C over a smart-HTTP remote on localhost:
`crustify/scripts/http-remote.py`, `git http-backend` behind an HTTP/1.1 front with persistent
connections, and `crustify/scripts/http-gate.sh` (proposal's item 11). The front frames each
response by its path: `Content-Length`, chunked in 1, 7, 4096 and 65536-byte chunks, chunked
with chunk extensions, close-delimited, or a header block llhttp refuses. One remote asks for
Basic credentials. The variant's `git2` cloned `testrepo.git` and a three-commit repository of
the source revision's tree through the first three framings, each clone's refs, HEAD, checkout
and `fsck --connectivity-only` checked. It also ran four clones that fail: close-delimited ("could
not read refs from remote repository"), malformed ("http parser error: Invalid header token",
the reason read through `llhttp_get_error_reason`), 404 and 401. Through each of the first three
framings, `libgit2_tests -sonline::push -sonline::clone::credentials` ran against the guarded
remote with `GITTEST_REMOTE_URL`, as libgit2's CI runs `auth_clone_and_push`, and passed 23 with
1 skipped. Gen2's C and gen3's Rust give the same `results.txt` on plain, ASan+UBSan and TSan, and
gen3's coverage variant gives it too: every outcome, every clone's refs, and the requests each
remote answered, by method, framing and status. No run printed a sanitizer report. On the
coverage variant, the run called 24 of the 31 exports, the chunk-extension dispatchers
included, and covered `api.rs`'s 128 of 175 lines and 31 of 44 functions. The seven it never
calls are `on_url` and `on_method` and their `_complete`s, which only a request parse calls,
`on_reset` and `llhttp_resume_after_upgrade`, which need pipelined or upgraded messages, and
`llhttp_finish`, which libgit2 calls only when the socket ends inside a body. The gateway's
`unit_priv` tests call six of them: `each_dispatcher_export_calls_its_own_slot` calls every
dispatcher and `llhttp_finish_returns_cs_codes` calls `llhttp_finish`. None calls
`llhttp_resume_after_upgrade`, whose body is `ParserMut::resume_after_upgrade` in a `barrier`;
`unit_pub`'s `resume_after_upgrade_clears_only_an_upgrades_pause` tests that method. The results are kept in the run dir
(`http-gate-results.txt`), for the switches of `http.c` and `llhttp.c` to compare with.

`c/` changed, so the crate was packaged as `package-gate-procedure` has it, with the workspace's
Git patch of ffibox, as at `opt.c`'s switch. It has 695 files, `api.c` out, and builds alone in
bundled mode, where `llhttp.c`'s dispatchers resolve to the Rust. Its `lib` tests: 843 pass, the
gateway's eight among them. The other 58 need the fixture repositories of `c/tests/resources`,
as at the two switches before.

From the switch on, the module's coverage is its Rust's, and the C figures lose `api.c`'s 283
lines. This run did not measure the workspace's coverage. What this switch shows the procedure
lacks is added to `crustify/evolution/module-switch-procedure` (items 10 to 13). The review
reproducer that enables the deleted feature (`wave-194/batch-7/equiv/execute-export-moves-an-empty-runs-error-pos`)
is left as it is, reproducing at the commit its report names. Usage cells are the assistant's.

### `git2/src/cli/opt.c` integration: the switch from C

The campaign's second switch, and the first of the `git2` link unit, the CLI. It was run by
`modules/git2/src/cli/opt.c/integration/run-1` on the module's branch, after the merge of the
working branch (`6d823f4d7`): `f68ea8660`, and the fork's `f57e1a616`. It followed
`utf8.c`'s procedure (`crustify/evolution/module-switch-procedure`) with its scripts unchanged.
The export feature `ffi-export-src-cli-opt-c` is deleted, so `opt.rs`'s gateway compiles from
now on, and its six `unit_priv` tests run in `lib`. No export feature is left. The CLI's
remaining C calls the five exports `cli_opt_parser_init`, `cli_opt_parser_next`,
`cli_opt_parse`, `cli_opt_foreach` and `cli_opt_status_fprint`: `main.c`, the `cmd_*.c`
commands, `common.c` and `opt_usage.c`. Their raw bindings stay and reach the exports. The
module binds no function without an export, so no allowlist entry goes. The types stay for the
layouts that C builds and reads. `src/cli/opt.c` leaves `c/` on the local `fork/main` as
`integrate src/cli/opt.c`, which is not pushed. `opt.h` stays for `common.h`. The module has no
tied C test. The exports are a private module's, so the crate's API does not change.

#!/bin/bash
# Build a generation of the target's variants from the C that remains (crustify's setup
# skill, Builds; porting-workflow, Builds): run after a module's switch removes C, and
# whenever the shared variants are rebuilt.
#
#   build-variants.sh <generation dir> [<variant>...]
#
# A generation is a directory beside crustify/builds, as crustify/builds.gen<n>, which a
# checkout's crustify/builds links to once it is built: it holds `c`, a detached worktree
# of this checkout's `c/` repository at the commit `c/` has checked out, which `c/` must
# hold without changes, and one build dir per variant of crustify/artifacts/build.json
# (every one by default), named as its `dir` names it. Each variant's `configure` and
# `build` commands run from its dir, physically resolved, so that the relative paths they
# take (the generation's `../c`, the side campaigns' installs four levels up) resolve as
# for the shared builds, with CRUSTIFY_ROOT set to this checkout, whose scripts the
# commands run and whose Rust the C consumers link. The variants build side by side, each
# logging to <dir>/crustify/build.log; the exit status is 1 when any fails, naming it.
# An existing generation is not rebuilt: a variant whose dir exists is refused.
set -euo pipefail
usage='usage: build-variants.sh <generation dir> [<variant>...]'
gen=${1:?$usage}
shift
root=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)
spec=$root/crustify/artifacts/build.json
mapfile -t all < <(python3 -I -c 'import json,sys; print("\n".join(json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))["variants"]))' "$spec")
variants=("$@")
[ ${#variants[@]} -gt 0 ] || variants=("${all[@]}")
for v in "${variants[@]}"; do
  printf '%s\n' "${all[@]}" | grep -qx -- "$v" || { echo "build-variants.sh: no variant $v in $spec" >&2; exit 2; }
done

mkdir -p "$gen"
gen=$(cd -P "$gen" && pwd)
commit=$(git -C "$root/c" rev-parse HEAD)
if [ ! -e "$gen/c" ]; then
  [ -z "$(git -C "$root/c" status --porcelain --untracked-files=no)" ] || {
    echo "build-variants.sh: $root/c has changes: a generation is built from a commit" >&2
    exit 1
  }
  git -C "$root/c" worktree add --detach "$gen/c" "$commit" >/dev/null
fi
held=$(git -C "$gen/c" rev-parse HEAD)
[ "$held" = "$commit" ] || {
  echo "build-variants.sh: $gen/c holds $held, not $root/c's $commit" >&2
  exit 1
}

field() { python3 -I -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))["variants"][sys.argv[2]][sys.argv[3]])' "$spec" "$1" "$2"; }

pids=() names=()
for v in "${variants[@]}"; do
  dir=$gen/$(basename "$(field "$v" dir)")
  [ ! -e "$dir" ] || { echo "build-variants.sh: $dir exists: a generation is built once" >&2; exit 1; }
  mkdir -p "$dir/crustify"
  configure=$(field "$v" configure)
  build=$(field "$v" build)
  (
    cd -P "$dir"
    export CRUSTIFY_ROOT=$root
    {
      echo "+ $configure"
      eval "$configure"
      echo "+ $build"
      eval "$build"
    } >"$dir/crustify/build.log" 2>&1
  ) &
  pids+=($!) names+=("$v")
done
failed=()
for i in "${!pids[@]}"; do
  wait "${pids[$i]}" || failed+=("${names[$i]}")
done
if [ ${#failed[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
  echo "build-variants.sh: ${failed[*]} failed: see each <dir>/crustify/build.log under $gen" >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "build-variants.sh: $gen holds ${variants[*]}, from c/ at $commit"

#!/bin/bash
# Build a generation of the target's variants from the C that remains (crustify's setup
# skill, Builds; porting-workflow, Builds): run after a module's switch removes C, and
# whenever the shared variants are rebuilt.
#
#   build-variants.sh <generation dir> [<variant>...]
#
# A generation is a directory beside crustify/builds, as crustify/builds.gen<n>, which a
# checkout's crustify/builds links to once it is built: it holds `c`, a detached worktree
# of this checkout's `c/` repository at the commit `c/` has checked out, which `c/` must
# hold without changes, and one build dir per variant of crustify/artifacts/build.json
# (every one by default), named as its `dir` names it. Each variant's `configure` and
# `build` commands run from its dir, physically resolved, so that the relative paths they
# take (the generation's `../c`, the side campaigns' installs four levels up) resolve as
# for the shared builds, with CRUSTIFY_ROOT set to this checkout, whose scripts the
# commands run and whose Rust the C consumers link. The variants build side by side, each
# logging to <dir>/crustify/build.log; the exit status is 1 when any fails, naming it.
# An existing generation is not rebuilt: a variant whose dir exists is refused.
set -euo pipefail
usage='usage: build-variants.sh <generation dir> [<variant>...]'
gen=${1:?$usage}
shift
root=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)
spec=$root/crustify/artifacts/build.json
mapfile -t all < <(python3 -I -c 'import json,sys; print("\n".join(json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))["variants"]))' "$spec")
variants=("$@")
[ ${#variants[@]} -gt 0 ] || variants=("${all[@]}")
for v in "${variants[@]}"; do
  printf '%s\n' "${all[@]}" | grep -qx -- "$v" || { echo "build-variants.sh: no variant $v in $spec" >&2; exit 2; }
done

mkdir -p "$gen"
gen=$(cd -P "$gen" && pwd)
commit=$(git -C "$root/c" rev-parse HEAD)
if [ ! -e "$gen/c" ]; then
  [ -z "$(git -C "$root/c" status --porcelain --untracked-files=no)" ] || {
    echo "build-variants.sh: $root/c has changes: a generation is built from a commit" >&2
    exit 1
  }
  git -C "$root/c" worktree add --detach "$gen/c" "$commit" >/dev/null
fi
held=$(git -C "$gen/c" rev-parse HEAD)
[ "$held" = "$commit" ] || {
  echo "build-variants.sh: $gen/c holds $held, not $root/c's $commit" >&2
  exit 1
}

field() { python3 -I -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))["variants"][sys.argv[2]][sys.argv[3]])' "$spec" "$1" "$2"; }

pids=() names=()
for v in "${variants[@]}"; do
  dir=$gen/$(basename "$(field "$v" dir)")
  [ ! -e "$dir" ] || { echo "build-variants.sh: $dir exists: a generation is built once" >&2; exit 1; }
  mkdir -p "$dir/crustify"
  configure=$(field "$v" configure)
  build=$(field "$v" build)
  (
    cd -P "$dir"
    export CRUSTIFY_ROOT=$root
    {
      echo "+ $configure"
      eval "$configure"
      echo "+ $build"
      eval "$build"
    } >"$dir/crustify/build.log" 2>&1
  ) &
  pids+=($!) names+=("$v")
done
failed=()
for i in "${!pids[@]}"; do
  wait "${pids[$i]}" || failed+=("${names[$i]}")
done
if [ ${#failed[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
  echo "build-variants.sh: ${failed[*]} failed: see each <dir>/crustify/build.log under $gen" >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "build-variants.sh: $gen holds ${variants[*]}, from c/ at $commit"

#!/bin/bash
# Build the safe crate's Rust static library for a variant's own C to link (crustify's
# porting-workflow skill, Builds): once a module has switched from C, the remaining C, its
# library, CLI and tests, reaches the module through the crate's exports, and its CMake
# build links this library (`LIBGIT2_RUST_LIBRARY`).
#
#   rust-staticlib.sh <variant> <archive>
#
# Run from the variant's build dir, configured and not yet built, as the first step of its
# `build` command in crustify/artifacts/build.json; <archive> is the library written,
# relative to the build dir, as its configure's `-DLIBGIT2_RUST_LIBRARY` names it. The crate
# is the one of the checkout this script belongs to, built as a `staticlib` on the dev
# profile, the campaign's tests' own, in campaign mode against this build dir
# (`CRUSTIFY_BUILD_DIR`) with `CRUSTIFY_STATICLIB` set, so that it reads the build's headers
# and configuration and links none of its C, and with the `bindgen` feature, so that the
# committed bindings are checked against them. Its Rust is instrumented as
# crustify/scripts/cargo-variant.sh instruments <variant>'s, so that one runtime serves the C
# and the Rust of every C consumer. Cargo's target dir is the build's own, `crustify/cargo`;
# the archive is replaced atomically, so that a link never reads a partial one.
set -euo pipefail
usage='usage: rust-staticlib.sh <variant> <archive>'
variant=${1:?$usage}
archive=${2:?$usage}
[ $# -eq 2 ] || { echo "$usage" >&2; exit 2; }
here=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)
host=x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
[ -f CMakeCache.txt ] && [ -f build.ninja ] || {
  echo "rust-staticlib.sh: $PWD is not a configured CMake build with the Ninja generator" >&2
  exit 2
}
build=$(pwd -P)
case $archive in /*) ;; *) archive=$build/$archive ;; esac

export CRUSTIFY_BUILD_DIR=$build CRUSTIFY_STATICLIB=1
export CARGO_TARGET_DIR=$build/crustify/cargo
crate=(-p libgit2-crustify --lib --locked --features bindgen)
bundled=
case $variant in
  plain)
    out=$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/debug
    "$here/crustify/scripts/cargo-variant.sh" "$variant" rustc "${crate[@]}" --crate-type staticlib ;;
  coverage|asan-ubsan|tsan)
    out=$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/$host/debug
    "$here/crustify/scripts/cargo-variant.sh" "$variant" rustc "${crate[@]}" --crate-type staticlib ;;
  bsan)
    # `cargo bsan` drives `build`, `run` and `test` only, and a `build` cannot change a
    # crate's type. It sets its rustc driver up and runs the cargo CARGO names, so a stand-in
    # for that cargo turns its `build` into `rustc --crate-type staticlib`, every other call,
    # its `metadata` among them, passing through. The /opt shim of `cargo bsan` sets CARGO
    # itself, so the real cargo-bsan, the ELF on PATH, is run directly, as the shim runs it.
    out=$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/bsan/$host/debug
    real_cargo=$(type -P cargo)
    real_bsan=
    for c in $(type -ap cargo-bsan); do
      [ "$(head -c4 "$c")" = $'\x7fELF' ] && { real_bsan=$c; break; }
    done
    [ -n "$real_bsan" ] || { echo "rust-staticlib.sh: no cargo-bsan executable on PATH" >&2; exit 1; }
    mkdir -p "$CARGO_TARGET_DIR"
    shim=$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/cargo-rustc-staticlib
    printf '%s\n' '#!/bin/bash' \
#!/bin/bash
# Run cargo against one crustify prebuild of libgit2, instrumenting Rust to match.
#
#   crustify/scripts/cargo-variant.sh <variant> <cargo subcommand> [args...]
#
# <variant> is a `variants` key of crustify/artifacts/build.json: plain, coverage, asan-ubsan,
# tsan or bsan. Each variant uses its own target dir under target/.
# The safe crate's build script, in campaign mode, links the variant's static archive (its
# `static` in build.json) into each test binary, so the C runs under the instrumentation the
# Rust is built with here, one runtime serving both. Set CRUSTIFY_BUILD_DIR to a private build
# of the variant, which carries the same archive, to link it instead of the shared one.
set -euo pipefail
variant=${1:?usage: cargo-variant.sh <variant> <cargo subcommand> [args...]}
shift
here=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)
host=x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
export CRUSTIFY_BUILD_VARIANT=$variant
export CARGO_TARGET_DIR=${CARGO_TARGET_DIR:-$here/target/$variant}
# pcre2-sys links the variant's side-campaign PCRE2, the one libgit2's C links, rather than
# building its vendored copy, which would shadow it in every test binary. The side campaigns'
# clones sit where the variant's build found their installs, beside the repository whose
# crustify/builds holds it (build.json's configure takes them from `$PWD/../../../..` in
# crustify/builds/<variant>): resolved physically through crustify/builds, which a worktree or
# a gate snapshot links to that repository's, so that every checkout finds the same ones.
side=$(realpath -m "$here/crustify/builds/$variant/../../../..")
export PKG_CONFIG_PATH="$side/pcre2-bindings/crustify/builds/$variant/install/lib/pkgconfig${PKG_CONFIG_PATH:+:$PKG_CONFIG_PATH}"
cd "$here"
# The nightly the workspace pins, for the sanitizers that need it.
nightly=$(sed -n 's/^nightly = "\(.*\)"$/\1/p' Cargo.toml)
# Cargo's own flags must come before a `--`, which hands the rest to the test binaries.
pre=() post=()
for arg in "$@"; do
  if [ ${#post[@]} -gt 0 ] || [ "$arg" = -- ]; then post+=("$arg"); else pre+=("$arg"); fi
done
case $variant in
  plain)
    exec cargo "$@" ;;
  coverage)
    # Source-based coverage on the pinned nightly, against the variant's clang-instrumented C,
    # which each test binary links statically, so that rustc's profiler runtime counts both;
    # crustify/scripts/coverage/ measures the suites as the testing spec's Coverage section does.
    export RUSTFLAGS="${RUSTFLAGS:-} -C instrument-coverage"
    export RUSTDOCFLAGS="${RUSTDOCFLAGS:-} -C instrument-coverage"
    export LLVM_PROFILE_FILE=${LLVM_PROFILE_FILE:-$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/profraw/%p-%m.profraw}
    exec cargo "+$nightly" "${pre[@]}" --target $host "${post[@]}" ;;
  asan-ubsan)
    export RUSTFLAGS="${RUSTFLAGS:-} -Zsanitizer=address -Cforce-frame-pointers=yes"
    export RUSTDOCFLAGS="${RUSTDOCFLAGS:-} -Zsanitizer=address"
    export ASAN_OPTIONS=${ASAN_OPTIONS:-detect_leaks=1:abort_on_error=1}
    export UBSAN_OPTIONS=${UBSAN_OPTIONS:-print_stacktrace=1:halt_on_error=1}

# crustify/builds holds it (build.json's configure takes them from `$PWD/../../../..` in
# crustify/builds/<variant>): resolved physically through crustify/builds, which a worktree or
# a gate snapshot links to that repository's, so that every checkout finds the same ones.

export PKG_CONFIG_PATH="$side/pcre2-bindings/crustify/builds/$variant/install/lib/pkgconfig${PKG_CONFIG_PATH:+:$PKG_CONFIG_PATH}"
cd "$here"
# The nightly the workspace pins, for the sanitizers that need it.
nightly=$(sed -n 's/^nightly = "\(.*\)"$/\1/p' Cargo.toml)
# Cargo's own flags must come before a `--`, which hands the rest to the test binaries.
pre=() post=()
for arg in "$@"; do
  if [ ${#post[@]} -gt 0 ] || [ "$arg" = -- ]; then post+=("$arg"); else pre+=("$arg"); fi
done
case $variant in
  plain)
    exec cargo "$@" ;;
  coverage)
    # Source-based coverage on the pinned nightly, against the variant's clang-instrumented C,
    # which each test binary links statically, so that rustc's profiler runtime counts both;
    # crustify/scripts/coverage/ measures the suites as the testing spec's Coverage section does.
    export RUSTFLAGS="${RUSTFLAGS:-} -C instrument-coverage"
    export RUSTDOCFLAGS="${RUSTDOCFLAGS:-} -C instrument-coverage"
    export LLVM_PROFILE_FILE=${LLVM_PROFILE_FILE:-$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/profraw/%p-%m.profraw}
    exec cargo "+$nightly" "${pre[@]}" --target $host "${post[@]}" ;;
  asan-ubsan)
    export RUSTFLAGS="${RUSTFLAGS:-} -Zsanitizer=address -Cforce-frame-pointers=yes"
    export RUSTDOCFLAGS="${RUSTDOCFLAGS:-} -Zsanitizer=address"
    export ASAN_OPTIONS=${ASAN_OPTIONS:-detect_leaks=1:abort_on_error=1}
    export UBSAN_OPTIONS=${UBSAN_OPTIONS:-print_stacktrace=1:halt_on_error=1}

## Legend

- `module` / `wave` / `batch` — the batch's place in `schedule.json`: its wave's module and
  the wave and batch indices
- `objective` — `wrap` or `port`; `pass` — `first` for a translation batch, `review` for a
  review batch; `Σ first` / `Σ review` total each pass apart
- `types` / `symbols` / `fields` — the batch's scheduled units (callbacks count as
  symbols) and its types' assigned field accessors; a review row counts what it reviewed
- `$` / `tokens` / `wall` — the agent's computed cost (API-equivalent under
  subscription), its tokens in millions as `crustify usage` reports them, and its elapsed
  time, C rebuild included; `$/<unit>` divides `$` by the row's units
- `+LoC` — the landing's Rust insertions/deletions; `loc` — its `.rs` insertions

#!/bin/bash
# run.sh <repo> <package> <cov dir>: build a coverage-instrumented scratch copy of the safe
# crate against the `coverage` variant, its test items under #[coverage(off)], and run each
# suite alone into <cov dir>/prof/<suite>: lib, each integration test binary, and doc. Each
# binary links the variant's C statically, so its profiles count the C and the Rust alike.
# report.py then reads the figures (testing spec, Coverage), with the variant's static archive
# as the C object.
set -euo pipefail
repo=$1 pkg=$2 out=$3
host=x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
nightly=$(sed -n 's/^nightly = "\(.*\)"$/\1/p' "$repo/Cargo.toml")
tree=$out/tree
rm -rf "$out"; mkdir -p "$tree/crustify" "$out/prof"
(cd "$repo" && tar -cf - --exclude=./target --exclude=./crustify --exclude=./c --exclude=./.git .) | (cd "$tree" && tar -xf -)
ln -s "$repo/c" "$tree/c"
ln -s "$repo/crustify/artifacts" "$tree/crustify/artifacts"
ln -s "$repo/crustify/builds" "$tree/crustify/builds"
python3 "$(dirname "$0")/mark.py" "$tree/src" "$tree/src/lib.rs"
cd "$tree"
export CRUSTIFY_BUILD_VARIANT=coverage CARGO_TARGET_DIR=$out/target
export RUSTFLAGS="-C instrument-coverage" RUSTDOCFLAGS="-C instrument-coverage -Z unstable-options --persist-doctests $out/doctests"
cargo "+$nightly" test -p "$pkg" --target $host --no-run --message-format=json 2>"$out/build.err" \
  | python3 -c 'import sys,json
for l in sys.stdin:
  try: d=json.loads(l)
  except: continue
  if d.get("reason")=="compiler-artifact" and d.get("executable") and d["target"]["kind"]!=["custom-build"] and d.get("profile",{}).get("test"): print(d["target"]["name"],d["target"]["kind"][0],d["executable"])' > "$out/bins.txt"
cat "$out/bins.txt"
while read -r name kind exe; do
  suite=$([ "$kind" = lib ] && echo lib || echo "$name")
  mkdir -p "$out/prof/$suite"
  echo "== $suite"
  LLVM_PROFILE_FILE="$out/prof/$suite/%p-%m.profraw" "$exe" --skip compile_fail > "$out/$suite.log" 2>&1 || echo "rc=$? in $suite"
  tail -3 "$out/$suite.log"
  "$exe" --list 2>/dev/null | grep -c ': test$' > "$out/$suite.count" || true
done < "$out/bins.txt"
mkdir -p "$out/prof/doc"
echo "== doc"
LLVM_PROFILE_FILE="$out/prof/doc/%p-%m.profraw" cargo "+$nightly" test -p "$pkg" --target $host --doc > "$out/doc.log" 2>&1 || echo "rc=$? in doc"
tail -3 "$out/doc.log"
"""report.py <cov dir> <name>=<dir>[:<dir>...][@<compilation dir>],... --c <C object>...

Merges each suite's profiles under <cov dir>/prof/, the four suites' union as TOTAL and every
suite's as ALL, and prints the TOTAL line of `llvm-cov report` for each named scope, with the C
objects and every test and doctest binary as objects for every suite. A scope's @<dir>
resolves the relative paths a C build recorded. MERGED=1 reuses the merged profiles, and ONLY=<suite> reports that one alone.

A scope written `<name>=@c`, such as `C=@c`, reads the C objects alone, with no source filter:
the archive holds only the link unit's TUs, whatever paths their build recorded. Any other
scope fails when a file it reports lies outside its dirs: llvm-cov falls back to every object
when its filters match no source, which would count the test binaries' std and Rust as C.

The C objects are those of the coverage variant's static archive, its `static` in build.json
(crustify/builds/coverage/crustify/libcrustify.a), which the test binaries link: each binary holds
only the TUs it reaches, so the archive, which llvm-cov reads member by member, gives every TU
its place in the denominator, one no test reaches at zero."""
import subprocess,sys,pathlib,json,glob,os
out0=pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1])
nightly=os.environ.get("NIGHTLY") or next(l.split('"')[1] for l in open(out0/"tree"/"Cargo.toml") if l.startswith("nightly = "))
sysroot=subprocess.run(['rustc','+'+nightly,'--print','sysroot'],capture_output=True,text=True,check=True).stdout.strip()
B=sysroot+'/lib/rustlib/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/bin/'
out=pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1]); scopes=dict(s.split('=',1) for s in sys.argv[2].split(','))
cobjs=sys.argv[sys.argv.index('--c')+1:]
bins=[l.split()[2] for l in (out/'bins.txt').read_text().splitlines()]
docs=[p for p in glob.glob(str(out/'doctests'/'**'/'rust_out'),recursive=True)]
objs=cobjs+bins+docs
suites=sorted(p.name for p in (out/'prof').iterdir() if any(p.glob('*.profraw')))
def merge(name,dirs):
    raws=[str(r) for d in dirs for r in (out/'prof'/d).glob('*.profraw')]
    prof=out/f'{name}.profdata'
    subprocess.run([B+'llvm-profdata','merge','-sparse','-o',str(prof)]+raws,check=True)
    return prof
def total(prof,srcs):
    cd=[]
    if srcs==['@c']: use,srcs=cobjs,[]
    else:
        use=objs
        if '@' in srcs[-1]: srcs[-1],c=srcs[-1].split('@'); cd=['-compilation-dir='+c]
    args=[B+'llvm-cov','report','-instr-profile',str(prof)]+cd+[use[0]]+sum((['-object',o] for o in use[1:]),[])+srcs
    r=subprocess.run(args,capture_output=True,text=True)

---
name: ffimap
description: "Deterministic counts and sites of a Rust crate's unsafe and FFI surface. Read before a batch lands (its safe-boundary scan and safety-audit cells), before planning an audit's worksets, and when reviewing for unsafety, contracts or UB."
---

# ffimap

ffimap maps a Rust crate's FFI and unsafe surface deterministically: a rustc driver over
HIR and typeck counts unsafe blocks and fns, raw and void pointers by position and
visibility, FFI calls and wrapper use. No model is involved, so two runs over one tree
agree exactly. Its `--help` lists its flags, and its `docs/schema.md`, read in full before
its first scan, its counters and how a report combines them.

It counts what the build compiles of the safe crate itself, and prints one JSON document:

```bash
ffimap <workdir> > <file>.json
```

Every scan names the crate's seams, the functions that hand a value between its wrapper and
its raw form, so that each counter's `of_which.seam` share tells that plumbing apart from
the pointer management a consumer of the safe API faces: ffibox's handle seams `as_ptr`,
`as_mut_ptr`, `as_void_ptr`, `from_ptr` and `from_void_ptr`, the ownership hand-offs
`from_raw_parts`, `into_raw_parts`, `into_raw`, `from_c`, `into_c` and `as_c_ptr`, the adoption of a raw C
value, `from_raw`, and the view of a C object as another, `as_object`. A crate built on
ffibox is scanned with `--ffibox`, and its `-sys` crates are named with `--sys-crates`:

```bash
ffimap <workdir> --ffibox --sys-crates <the -sys crates> --regions ffi_import,ffi_export \
    --seams as_ptr,as_mut_ptr,as_void_ptr,from_ptr,from_void_ptr,from_raw_parts,into_raw_parts,into_raw,from_c,into_c,as_c_ptr,from_raw,as_object \
    > <file>.json
```

In a port campaign, a scan names with `--features` the export feature of every module not
yet switched, as the [conventions](../../rust/conventions/SKILL.md)' Export features section
names them, so that the `ffi_export` gateways compiled under them are counted. Every scan
names the module's unsafe regions, as the conventions' Unsafe regions section names them,
with `--regions`.

Two scans are compared only when they name the same seams, regions and features.

Its counters form one tree, each named by its dotted path into the scan's `counts`, as
ffimap's `docs/schema.md` describes; a metric is a counter, or a combination of counters
that schema allows: a partition's leaves summed, a share read against the record it cuts,
or subtracted from it. `--sites <counter> ...` also lists where each named counter's
increments are, and takes leaves only, such as `fn.unsafe.pub`; the workspace is named
before it. The counters that recur:

- `fn.unsafe.pub`, the public `unsafe fn`s, the crate's public unsafe surface, of which
  `fn.unsafe.of_which.other.pub` are those neither a trait nor a seam required; and
  `raw_ptr.fn_sig_arg.unsafe.pub` and `raw_ptr.fn_sig_ret.unsafe.pub`, the raw pointers in
  their signatures;
- `raw_ptr.field.pub`, `raw_ptr.fn_sig_arg.safe.pub` and `raw_ptr.fn_sig_ret.safe.pub`, the
  raw pointers in public fields and in the signatures of public safe fns, together
  `raw_ptr.total.safe.pub`, the raw pointers on the safe public interface; and their
  `of_which.void` shares, the type-erased ones among them;
- `ty.ffibox.wrapper.as.borrowed.std.{pub,priv}`, the references to a cell, less their
  `of_which.self_in_ref_accessor` and `of_which.self_in_trait_impl` shares, the positions
  ffibox sanctions: references to C memory where a handle belongs, which assert `noalias`,
  `readonly` or validity over memory C may write; `ty.ffibox.sys.as.borrowed.std`, the same
  of the raw C structs; and `raw_ptr.casted_to.std.{borrow,slice,string}`, the borrows,
  slices and strings formed from a raw pointer, over bytes C must neither free nor change
  while they live;
- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.send.{pub,priv}` and `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.sync.{pub,priv}`,
  each an unchecked assertion that a value may move to or be shared with another thread;
- `raw_ptr.deref.wr` and `raw_ptr.deref.rd`, raw-pointer writes and reads, each a pointer
  the implementer vouches is non-null, aligned, live, initialized and unaliased by a live
  reference; and
- `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.impl_drop.{pub,priv}` and
  `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.impl_clone.{pub,priv}`, the types that hold a raw pointer and
  tear it down or copy it by hand, and `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.none.{pub,priv}`, those
  that declare nothing about it. Each of these five also has a `.total`, the sum of its two
  leaves, which is no leaf for `--sites`.

ffimap is neither complete nor sound: its sites are where review starts, not all it
covers. It does not count the lifetimes formed inside `unsafe` blocks, such as a reference
or lifetime-annotated handle made from a raw pointer by `&*p`, `from_ptr`, `from_raw` or
`from_raw_parts`, or changed by a `transmute`: those are found in the source.

What follows is how ffimap serves each stage: each section names the skill and section it
adds to, and states only what ffimap adds there.

## Binding and porting

### Binding › Safe boundary

Before a batch lands, a scan with `--sites fn.unsafe.pub raw_ptr.field.pub
raw_ptr.fn_sig_arg.safe.pub raw_ptr.fn_sig_ret.safe.pub` lists the public
`unsafe fn`s and the raw pointers on the safe public interface, and each of those sites
that belongs to the batch's changeset and that a safe variant could replace is fixed.
Its `--sites` also name the unsafe code outside both regions,
`code.unsafe_block.of_which.outside_regions`, another crate's macro expansions included,
which the `unsafe_code` lint misses, and `fn.unsafe.of_which.outside_regions.pub` and
`.priv`: outside the raw bindings, each of those sites in the batch's changeset is moved
into its region.

## Accounting

### Accounting › Landing cells

A batch's row in the dashboard's `Batches: safety audit` table is the change in each of
the Safety audit's metrics, from a scan of the tip its landing rebased onto to a scan of
the tree it lands.

### Accounting › API stability

`ffimap api` measures a safe crate's consumer-facing API per C item, from rustdoc JSON, as
its `docs/api.md` describes, read in full before its first use. A C item is the
`<kind>::<path>` of a `Wraps` or `Replaces` anchor, its surface every stand-in the anchor
names and the handles and owners tied to it, each judged by the contract
[`binding-types`](../../rust/binding/types/SKILL.md)' Safe layout section gives a consumer:
the methods every form offers, its reborrows and dereferences, and the traits a consumer
can use, never a form's raw access or seams. A batch generates the safe crate's rustdoc
JSON on the tip its landing rebased onto and on the tree it lands, with a nightly whose
`format_version` the tool supports, and ffibox's, with private items, for the contracts of
the forms it defines:

```bash
cargo +<nightly> rustdoc -p <crate> --lib -- -Z unstable-options --output-format json
ffimap api diff <base>.json <tree>.json --dep <ffibox>.json --items "<the worklist's keys>" --format json
```

Each item comes out `kept`, `extended`, `changed`, `removed` or `new`, with its anchor's
move from `Wraps` to `Replaces` where a port made it. The batch's row in the dashboard's
`Batches: API stability` table counts them over its worklist, and over the crate's
unattributed public items, compared per module.

### Accounting › Records

An unseeded scan of the unsafe and FFI surface is recorded at each batch's, wave's and
the campaign's end, as `ffimap.json` in its artifact directory: a batch's in the run dir
of the run that landed it, a wave's in its wave's dir, as `layout` spells it, and the
campaign's in `crustify/artifacts/`. A module's end is the scan of the last wave of its `wrap` and `port` items.

## Reviewing

### Reviewing › Objectives

A review locates the sites of its objectives with a scan, `--sites` with their counters,
and keeps those in its workset: the code its commits add or change, or its modules and
the types, trait impls and functions they name.

- `unsafety`: `fn.unsafe.pub`, `raw_ptr.field.pub`, `raw_ptr.fn_sig_arg.safe.pub` and
  `raw_ptr.fn_sig_ret.safe.pub`.
- `contracts`: `fn.unsafe.pub`, `raw_ptr.fn_sig_arg.unsafe.pub` and
  `raw_ptr.fn_sig_ret.unsafe.pub`, whose `# Safety` obligations are evaluated.
- `ub`: these smells first, in this order:
  1. references into C memory: the references to a cell outside its sanctioned positions,
     `ty.ffibox.wrapper.as.borrowed.std.{pub,priv}` less those shares, and to a raw C
     struct, `ty.ffibox.sys.as.borrowed.std.{pub,priv}`, then
     `raw_ptr.casted_to.std.{borrow,slice,string}`;
  2. thread-safety claims, `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.send.{pub,priv}` and
     `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.sync.{pub,priv}`, checked against
     the C library's contract: a data race is reachable from safe code when the library
     does not allow what they assert;
  3. the lifetimes formed inside `unsafe` blocks, found in the source: unsound when the
     handle can outlive the owner of the memory or the point at which C frees or
     invalidates it;
  4. raw pointers a consumer can set, `raw_ptr.fn_sig_arg.safe.pub` and
     `raw_ptr.field.pub`, with their `of_which.void` shares: unsound when a safe path
     dereferences or frees what the consumer passed or stored;
  5. raw-pointer dereferences, `raw_ptr.deref.wr` then `raw_ptr.deref.rd`: first in the
     modules that also hold references into C memory, where a write may invalidate a
     reference, and outside a type's accessors; and
  6. hand-written teardown and copies, `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.impl_drop.{pub,priv}`
     and `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.impl_clone.{pub,priv}`.

## Audit

### Audit workflow › Worksets

The audit's worksets are planned from a scan of the crate, run once each build
configuration it audits is in place, with `--sites` over the counters of its objectives.
A file outside every configuration scanned has no sites, and is planned from its source.

For `ub`, the modules that hold the smells ffimap's review guidance lists for `ub` are
reviewed first, in that order; for `contracts`, those that hold the crate's unsafe API and
its justifications, the `contracts` counters above. The rest of the crate
follows the smells.

The modules are batched by their sites, and a module that is split keeps a type, trait
impl or function with its sites in one batch. A site of `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.impl_drop`,
`.impl_clone`, `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.send` or `.sync`, at either leaf, is a trait impl, named
`Drop for <type>`, `Clone for <type>`, `Send for <type>` or `Sync for <type>`. Each review
runs the same scan over its own modules, so the sites are not passed on.
